text: It's three A.M. You wake up...
but you can't move.
You can't move a finger. You can't scream.
Then... you feel something watching you.
In the corner of your room... something is standing.
It's coming closer. Closer. And closer.
Until it sits... right on your chest.
What do you do? A: you shut your eyes. B: you look at it.
Whatever you choose...
But here's what most people don't know.
It's not a ghost. It's called sleep paralysis.
When you sleep, your brain paralyzes your body, so you don't act out your dreams.
But sometimes, your mind wakes up before your body does.
You're awake, but your brain is still dreaming. That's why you see the shadow.
And here's the creepy part: people all over the world see the same shadow.
In the Philippines, it's the batibat. In Japan, kanashibari. In Canada, the Old Hag.
About eight in every hundred people have felt it.
If it happens to you: don't fight it. Wiggle your toes, and breathe slowly.
It will pass.
So tonight, before you fall asleep... check the corner first.
Comment YES if it's happened to you.
